system_overview: This specification models the Yo-Yo leader election algorithm with pruning for connected undirected graphs. It extends the base algorithm by adding graph pruning during the upward phase to remove redundant edges and nodes, ensuring the algorithm terminates when the sole remaining source becomes isolated and declares itself leader. All other nodes become inactive.
actors_and_components: The participants are nodes in a connected undirected graph, each with a unique integer identity. Nodes are dynamically classified as leaders (isolated source with no neighbors), sources (only outgoing edges), sinks (only incoming edges), or internal nodes (both). Nodes communicate via directed edges carrying two types of messages: downward messages with a value and upward messages with a yes/no reply and a prune flag.
state_variables: The system tracks five pieces of state per node: (1) an activation flag indicating whether the node is still participating, (2) the current phase (downward or upward), (3) the set of incoming neighbors, (4) the set of outgoing neighbors, and (5) a mailbox of pending messages. Messages in the upward phase carry an additional boolean flag indicating whether the receiving node should prune the corresponding edge.
initial_state: All nodes start active and in the downward phase. Edges are oriented from smaller to larger identity. All mailboxes are empty.
actions: The algorithm operates in rounds of downward and upward phases, as in the base version, but the upward phase includes pruning. During the downward phase, active source nodes broadcast their identity to outgoing neighbors; active non-source nodes wait for all incoming downward messages, then forward the minimum value to outgoing neighbors. During the upward phase, pruning rules apply: (1) A sink node with only a single incoming neighbor becomes inactive and is removed from the graph, since it contributes no useful information. (2) When a node receives the same value from multiple incoming neighbors (indicating redundant paths from the same source), it non-deterministically keeps one sender per distinct value and marks the others for pruning. Upward messages include a prune flag that tells the receiver to drop the corresponding edge. Source nodes process upward replies by reversing edges for 'no' responses and removing edges marked for pruning. The combined effect of edge reversal and pruning progressively simplifies the graph until only the minimum-identity node remains as an isolated leader.
safety_properties: A neighbor consistency invariant accounts for edges being reversed ('no' messages pending) or pruned (prune-flagged messages pending). Type correctness ensures all variables remain in expected domains. A property checks that deadlock occurs if and only if the termination condition holds.
liveness_properties: The algorithm eventually terminates: the minimum-identity node becomes the leader (isolated with no neighbors), all other nodes become inactive, and all mailboxes are empty.
model_bounds: The graph topology is provided as constants. The model-checking configuration uses a five-node graph with specific edges. Deadlock checking is disabled since the algorithm terminates by reaching a deadlock state.
additional_assumptions: The specification assumes the graph is connected and undirected with no self-loops, and all node identities are distinct integers. Weak fairness is assumed on the next-state action. The pruning variant may create new source nodes (unlike the base algorithm), which is expected behavior as the graph is simplified.
